What's a single event or moment, good or bad, that forever changed your life? In what ways did it change you? [serious]

It's 1986 and there are two girls at a party standing next to each other that I'm interested in. One blonde, one with raven black hair. I chose the one on the right. Everything changed.

Had I picked the blonde girl, we would have had a good time, then moved on. I would have moved on when college started, having a good career as a lawyer. Eventually I would have met someone to marry, settled down and lived a very nice upper middle class life.

Instead I went right. We fell madly in love in one of those toxic and explosive kinds of relationships. I decided against moving out of state for her, and decided to go to a lesser school for journalism. We would both drop college entirely, deciding instead to just get married. She left me for another man two months before the marriage, moving all her belongings out of the apartment while I was at work as a bartender. I wouldn't see her again for twenty three years.

Well, I tried finding solace at the bottom of a bottle. I sought release in drugs. I packed what I had and hit the road. I would spend the next five years hitch hiking. I worked as a juggler, a fortune teller, a carnival barker, a farmer, a shaman, a repo man, a drug dealer and a beggar. Hell, I worked a hundred jobs, and lived in so many cities I can't keep track. I got to drink my full of the world.

Eventually I settled down. I became a family man. Worked as a game designer, a teacher, a writer. I've been rich, and I've been poor. My years on the road taught me more than I could have learned in a lifetime at school. By going mad, I became sane.

I know there's another version of myself. He chose the woman on the left. He never lived in a monastery, or walked across America. He never spent weeks in sweat lodges, taking compounds that would let him touch the divine. He had never gotten to taste the feeling of certain death. I don't think he fell in love with the world like I am. I worry about him, really. What a drab life.

true story. this was about early to mid 90s, back when bullying didn't have as bad of a wrap as it does now. i played basketball for the school and was pretty popular because of it. i lived in a small town with a population less than 2k. in 6th grade there was a young girl, a grade or two below me, that went to the same church i went to. i had almost no interaction with her, but would occasionally see her at school or church.

one day during lunch outside, there was about 6-8 of the school's most popular kids hovering around this girl. i walked closer to overhear them making fun of her because she had painted her shoes bright neon orange. the kids were brutal. my heart went out to her and i remember feeling like i should intervene. i gathered my courage and walked into the center of the group of the kids pointing, laughing, and kicking dust at her. i asked her if she was okay and told her i liked her shoes. the kids were stunned and i told them to leave her alone because she was my friend. they said a few more words and dispersed. she looked up at me and didn't say a thing.

8 years later her mother pulled my mom aside at church and brought up the incident and said that her daughter was contemplating suicide and that she was bullied so much during that time that she didn't feel like she wanted to live anymore. her mom said that that single act of kindness, just the few moments i spent to stand up for her, gave her enough reason to want to live and saved her life.

since that day in the schoolyard, i've felt compelled to stand up for the underdog and have consciously tried to include them in the things i do. when my mother told me what she had heard from the girl's mother, i knew i did the right thing.

For me, I've got two.

The first one is when I was 16. My fiancee (we planned to marry when I turned 18) died from complications after being shot. Now, I had heard prior to that that I was "too young to be in love" and "it's just puppy love" etc. Well, if felt real enough, and when she died, it fucked me over. No other woman had any real chance after that. I was emotionally numb for years afterward. I was a shitty boyfriend to every girl/woman I was with from that point forward. I didn't try to be damaged goods, I just couldn't really be open with anyone after that. Always guarded. I also became rather narcissistic. I eventually got married. And I did feel love for my wife. But something was always missing. To this day, 23 years later, I'm still not able to be 100% open to anyone except...

The second thing that changed me forever was the birth of my kids. When my daughter was born, something kind of let loose. When I looked at her for the first time, I felt something inside.. .shift? It's hard to put into words, but it was like a flood gate opened in me. All at once I knew that I could not just live for me anymore. I had someone that needed me and I needed to step up and actually be part of a family. I cried for the 1st time since Jolene died. My wife thought, and still does afaik (she's now an ex) it was just "tears of joy"- dad tears. And she was partially right. In that moment, I felt a combination of joy for my daughter, grief/regret over the shit-hole of a person I'd become, but most of all, relief. After that, for a few months, I cried at all sorts of shit. I cried when Mufasa dies in the damned Lion King. I'd seen that movie 50 times before, never gave a shit. But this time, I thought "What if that were me? What if daughter's name had to grow up without me?". It felt weird and foreign to give a shit about someone other than myself. Two years later we had a son. Both of my kids are amazing and I love them 100%.

It didn't work out with my wife and I. It turns out that we weren't compatible. I blame myself for that. I wasn't "healthy" in the mind when we started going out or even after we got married. We lasted a total of 12 years with a couple short breakups here and there. Neither of us have any regrets about it though, we got two amazing kids out of the ordeal. My daughter just turned 18 and is going to start school to become a veterinarian this fall.
